data.name: Aretas
data.gender_notes: Aretas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Aramaic word ‘arayt’, meaning ‘noble’, ‘virtuous’, or ‘exalted’. In the Bible, Aretas is mentioned as the name of the Arab king of Damascus, who married Herodias, the wife of his brother-in-law Herod Antipas. This marriage led to John the Baptist's execution, which ultimately brought about the downfall of Aretas' reign.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes nobility and virtue in one's actions and character.
data.etymology: Aretas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Noble, Virtuous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aretas total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Aretas, as a name, carries the impression of nobility and virtue, which is intertwined with Middle Eastern and biblical history. It highlights the importance of embracing moral values and demonstrates the lasting impact that significant characters, even those with controversial life choices, can have on our lives and history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Aretas serves as a reminder of the spiritual battle between good and evil and the importance of staying true to our values, no matter the personal cost. It also highlights how our actions, even seemingly small ones, can have far-reaching consequences. Ultimately, Aretas embodies the virtuous pursuit of living a life that uplifts others and strives for righteousness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Aretas, meaning "noble, exalted," embodies the Christian ideal of living a virtuous life rooted in humility, wisdom, and courage. This name calls forth the inner strength and nobility of the spirit to shine brightly in the world.

biblical_reference.note: Aretas was the king of the Arabs who opposed the rebuilding of the Jerusalem Temple in the time of the Prophet Ezra.

historical_references.reference: King Aretas IV of Nabataea, 9 BC – AD 40, ruled over the Nabataean Kingdom in the Arabian Peninsula.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Aretas remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Aretas from Jerusalem, Israel embodies the meaning of Aretas - "Noble, Virtuous". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
